lessonRef.title: Independent application A: compound growth and volatility

objective: Learners compute invented compound growth over five periods and contrast it with a sequence of equal-sized gains and losses.
scenario: Saoirse is an invented eighth grader modelling $10,000.00 two ways: growing at 8% a year for five simulated years, and a volatile pair of years rising 30% then falling 30%. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Grow Saoirse's invented $10,000.00 at 8% a year for five years, compounding annually.

prompts.text: What is the balance after five years at 8%?

tasks.directions: Now model Saoirse's volatile pair: a 30% rise in year one, then a 30% fall applied to the new balance.

prompts.text: What is the balance after the 30% rise?
What is the balance after the following 30% fall?

tasks.directions: Quantify the net effect of Saoirse's volatile pair and compare it with two steady years at 8%.

prompts.text: How much is lost across the volatile pair of years?
What would two steady years at 8% have produced?

tasks.directions: A 30% gain and a 30% loss did not cancel out.

prompts.text: Explain why equal percentage moves in opposite directions leave Saoirse worse off, and what that implies about recovering from a loss.

remediation: If a learner applies both percentages to the original amount, mark the base for each step in Saoirse's sequence before computing.
extension: After submitting the graded work, change one invented amount or assumption in the scenario. Rework the affected response using integer cents whenever money is involved, then explain whether and why the written judgment changes. Keep the variation fictional and do not use real household information.

items.promptText: What is the balance after five years at 8%?
What is the balance after the 30% rise?
What is the balance after the following 30% fall?
How much is lost across the volatile pair of years?
What would two steady years at 8% have produced?
Explain why equal percentage moves in opposite directions leave Saoirse worse off, and what that implies about recovering from a loss.
